source: Chosen on 2026-09-11 from the research in runs/2026-09-11-angular-structure-research-1 and C:/Obsidian/Notes 2025/Lely/Angular migratie/analyses/2026-09-11-angular-target-structure.md; state and hooks are placed by usage instead of all in core and shared.
note: Ordered rule list, first match wins. Every rule is data: no rule asks a person about an individual file. `outcome` is `move` (an Angular counterpart is created at `target`), `stay` (framework-agnostic, Angular imports the React file where it is), `retire` (a React-only construct with no Angular counterpart, such as a re-export barrel or a styled-components theme) or `merge` (a React file whose single Angular counterpart another rule already names; merges are left out of collision detection). A rule with `placeByUsage` takes `oneDomain` when every file that uses the React original sits in one domain, and `otherwise` when it is used across domains or by nothing but the shell. A test goes with the file it tests (the file with its name in the test's folder or in the parent of `__tests__`): it lands at `<folder of that file's target>/__tests__/<that target's name>.spec.ts`, so `useJunoSettings.test.tsx` becomes `juno-settings.store.spec.ts`, or it takes that file's `stay` or `retire`; only a test with no such file is matched by the rules. A file already under `root` is Angular code in place and no rule applies to it. scripts/angular-structure.mjs applies these rules and scripts/migration-map.mjs --measure reports every file they leave unmatched or send to the same path.

placeholders.{domain}: resolved through the table named by `domainFrom.table`, or for `placeByUsage` the one domain every user of the file sits in
placeholders.{page}: the page folder named by the `pageDomain` table entry
placeholders.{feature}: the React feature-folder segment, kebab-cased, with a trailing `Page` removed (`overviewPage` -> `overview`)
placeholders.{rest}: every path segment after the matched prefix, kebab-cased, with the file renamed by `nameStyle`
placeholders.{file}: only the renamed file of `{rest}`, dropping the carried folders

nameStyles.auto: `X.tsx` -> `x.component.ts`; `index.tsx` -> `<folder>.component.ts`, unless another file in the folder already carries the folder's name, which makes it a re-export barrel and retires it; `useX.ts(x)` -> `x.service.ts`; `X.styles.ts` -> `x.component.css`; `X.stories.tsx` -> `x.stories.ts`; `X.test.ts(x)` with no file it tests -> `__tests__/x.spec.ts`; `X.logic.ts` -> `utils/x.logic.ts`; `IX.ts`/`X.types.ts` -> `models/x.model.ts`; `EX.ts` -> `enums/x.enum.ts`; any other `.ts` helper -> `utils/x.ts`. Folders are kebab-cased and carried over; `__test__` is normalised to `__tests__`.
nameStyles.service: `useX.ts(x)` and a `useX/index.ts` folder entry -> `x.service.ts`, other files as `auto`
nameStyles.page: `XPage.tsx` -> `x.component.ts` directly in the domain's page folder, no extra component folder
nameStyles.keep: file name kebab-cased, extension forced to `.ts`, nothing else added
nameStyles.asis: file name unchanged; applied by `preprocess` to files that are already Angular

reactBoundness.purpose: Only rules with a `when.reactBound` condition use it. It decides whether an infrastructure file needs an Angular counterpart at all.
reactBoundness.source: Computed by scripts/migration-map.mjs from the product's value-import graph: a file is React-bound when it is .tsx, value-imports a React package, or value-imports a React-bound file. A test or story takes the outcome of the file it tests.

usage.purpose: Decides `placeByUsage`: the domains of the files that use a React original, found by walking its importers up until each path reaches a file with a domain.
usage.reason: The shell composes every provider; composing is wiring, not use, and counting it would send all state to core.

preprocess.note: Files already written under the provisional rule (project-constants.md:150-160) sit in an `angular\` folder beside their React parent. Before the rules are applied, that segment is removed from the path, so the file lands where its React parent's rule sends it. A `.ts` island file keeps its name (it is already Angular-named); a `.tsx` file in that folder is the React host that mounts the island, so it is not Angular code at all and only moves one folder up, staying in React.
preprocess.reason: This is what makes the provisional `angular\` folders a relocation rather than a rewrite, and it keeps the Angular root free of `.tsx`, which is what lets the compiler select Angular files by path prefix.

Constant values are framework-agnostic (folder-structure-en.md:86-87).
Constants have a dedicated technical folder (folder-structure-en.md:86-87).
A React provider plus its reader hook collapse into one Angular service; both React files map onto the counterpart `provider-translation` already names, so this is a merge, not a collision.
i18n is app-wide technical infrastructure (folder-structure-en.md:19).
The risk SignalR hubs are an app-wide singleton, not a helper (HorizonUICodeReview.md:92; 2026-09-11-codebase-decomposition-research.md:92-95).
Pure helpers import nothing React-bound and are reused as-is (2026-09-11-codebase-decomposition-research.md:483-487).

`shared/ui` holds generic UI primitives; the split with `src/components` is pre-existing React fragmentation and is not carried over (2026-09-11-codebase-decomposition-research.md:509-515).
Icon data and names are framework-agnostic.
Icon components are shared presentational components (HorizonUICodeReview.md:116-121).
Global style helpers stay shared (folder-structure-en.md:111-112).
The keyboard-shortcut registry is shared behaviour, not a component (project-constants.md:144-148).
A styled-components theme provider has no Angular counterpart; the first slice already reads `@lely/tokens` CSS custom properties directly (project-constants.md:96-101).
The styled-components theme helper disappears with styled-components.
Enums and small utilities inside the component folder are framework-agnostic (2026-09-11-codebase-decomposition-research-2.md:244,253).
Design-system primitives are reusable across every domain (HorizonUICodeReview.md:115-121).
A generic form control is a shared component, not a feature; files belong in the folder that matches their role (HorizonUICodeReview.md:52).
A test lands with the component it covers (project-constants.md:181-185).
Files with no feature folder of their own are domain-wide components (2026-09-11-codebase-decomposition-research.md:185-187).
Every feature folder is a page of exactly one domain; the feature segment is carried so two pages of one domain cannot collide (HorizonUICodeReview.md:132-144).
Build-tool typing, not application code.

Widening it to every `.ts` under the root is a separate decision, to be taken when the first Angular service exists.
